title: Information Retrieval
tagline: Text processing, inverted indexes, compression, ranked retrieval, BM25, evaluation, web search and link analysis, learning to rank and dense retrieval
summary: Search engines find the handful of relevant documents among billions in a fraction of a second. This course explains how: text processing and inverted indexes, index construction and compression, ranked retrieval with the vector space model and BM25, the evaluation of search quality, web crawling and link analysis with PageRank, learning to rank, and the dense neural retrieval used alongside language models.

chapters.title: Documents and text processing
chapters.summary: Tokenisation, normalisation and stemming, and the statistics of text such as Zipf’s law.

chapters.title: Inverted indexes
chapters.summary: Building an inverted index, postings lists, and Boolean and phrase queries.

chapters.title: Index construction and compression
chapters.summary: Building indexes at scale and compressing postings with variable-byte and gamma codes.

chapters.title: Ranked retrieval and the vector space model
chapters.summary: Term weighting with tf–idf, cosine similarity and efficient top-k scoring.

chapters.title: Probabilistic retrieval and BM25
chapters.summary: The probability ranking principle, BM25 and language-model approaches to retrieval.

chapters.title: Evaluating search
chapters.summary: Relevance judgements, precision and recall, mean average precision and nDCG, and studies with users.

chapters.title: Web search and link analysis
chapters.summary: Crawling, duplicate detection, PageRank and HITS.

chapters.title: Learning to rank
chapters.summary: Ranking features, pointwise, pairwise and listwise learning, and click models.

chapters.title: Dense retrieval and semantic search
chapters.summary: Text embeddings, approximate nearest-neighbour search and retrieval for language models.
